content.markdown:
# Spatial prediction and adaptive sampling for sub-hectare salinity pockets near the Tisa

## Verified facts
- TloCare samples one point per 4 ha, but Tisa-area clients report sunflower failure where maps look good; denser sampling found saline pockets of 0.3–0.8 ha that the standard grid skips. [F1]
- The company says denser sampling means more field work, laboratory cost and longer delivery, and its NDVI-guided adaptive sampling failed because salinity is not clear in early-spring vegetation indices. [F2]
- TloCare holds GPS coordinates and laboratory results for about 18,000 points from the last ten years, and can devote two developers and one GIS specialist up to one-third time to new functions. [F3]
- Filipović lists joint projects with companies developing soil monitoring sensors or irrigation scheduling software; he is cautious about projects requiring more than 20% of working time on administrative tasks and prefers clear data-sharing agreements. [F4]
- Filipović’s geostatistical survey in the Bačka lowland found ESP hotspots >25% in 18% of area, concentrated in micro-depressions; it reports that single-depth sampling underestimates subsurface alkalisation extent by 30–40%. [F5]
- He mapped apparent electrical conductivity with EM38 and EM31 across 2,300 ha of the Tamiš–Bega interfluve, producing ECe maps with three salinisation classes covering 8%, 31% and 61% of the area. [F6]
- He trained random forest and gradient boosting classifiers to predict whether 1-ha parcels in the Bačka lowland met agronomic reclamation criteria. [F7]
- He calibrated and validated SALTMOD at Bečej and Novi Bečej; TloCare plans electrical-conductivity or near-infrared field sensing to offer denser coverage without proportional sampling-cost growth. [F8]

## Our inference
- The joint project is conditional: the material lists joint-project interest, but the researcher’s availability is not confirmed.
- The researcher’s evidence comes from Bačka and Tamiš–Bega, so transfer to Tisa floodplain parcels is likely only after held-out validation.
- The 18,000 points come from a 4-ha grid, so they may not label 0.3–0.8 ha pockets; dense validation sampling is likely needed, and surface-only prediction may miss deeper salinity.

## Proposed next steps
- First experiment (proposed): hold out several Tisa-area parcels, including Ravnica Agro near Novi Bečej if TloCare can arrange dense sampling, and train a spatial salinity-risk model only on TloCare’s historical 18,000 GPS/lab points plus covariates. Compare it with TloCare’s current 4-ha grid baseline and with the researcher’s geostatistical, EM-induction and machine-learning methods. Proposed researcher contribution: model design and validation; company contribution: data, field access and dense reference sampling. Measure hit rate for 0.3–0.8 ha saline pockets, false-positive rate, and depth-dependent salinity. Go/no-go: proceed only if the model finds at least one pocket the 4-ha grid misses, with a false-positive rate TloCare accepts, and if extra sampling is targeted rather than proportional across the parcel; otherwise stop before rollout. Proposed sequence: data audit, model training, dense validation, review.
- Before modelling, jointly audit the 18,000 historical GPS/lab records for depth, date, method and parcel coverage, and agree a data-sharing arrangement covering client parcel data; the material does not confirm these terms.
- After validation, compare electrical conductivity and near-infrared sensing as sampling guides under early-spring conditions, because the company has not chosen a sensor and early NDVI was weak.
- Define with TloCare the risk-score threshold that triggers denser sampling, so the workflow reduces extra samples relative to uniform densification while finding missed pockets.

## Open questions
- Can the researcher confirm availability for a joint project and state whether industrial PhD supervision is also of interest?
- Can TloCare provide a data-sharing agreement covering the 18,000 historical GPS/lab records and client parcel data before work starts?
- Which Tisa-area parcels, such as Ravnica Agro near Novi Bečej, can be densely sampled as validation sites, and what budget and time are available?
- Which field sensor route is planned first, electrical conductivity or near-infrared, and when would it become available?
- What spatial resolution and prediction accuracy must be reached before the workflow may guide field sampling, and can both sides confirm the stated time limits: under 20% administrative load for the researcher and one-third developer/GIS capacity for the company?
